facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: On that basis the trust is highly levered and thinly covered but de-risked by a year of debt reduction. Principal debt fell by 852,487 from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026, funded by net equity proceeds of 541,798, new net lease mortgage notes, asset sales and cash on hand. Gross leverage on LTM core EBITDA moved from 10.77x at FY2025 to 9.78x at the third quarter of 2026, and cash interest cover from 1.35x to 1.41x. Both are weak, and the LTM EBITDA still includes earnings of hotels that have since been sold, so forward leverage on the retained portfolio is likely worse than the LTM figure shows; that last point is analyst inference, not a reported number. Liquidity is thin in cash and rests on a single undrawn secured revolver that matures within nine months. The balance sheet is secured-heavy: secured principal of 2,927,322 is 63% of principal debt, a share calculated in the Calculations section.

facts.label: Interpretation: evidence, mechanism and credit implication
facts.text: Leverage. Evidence: principal debt of 4,652,322 and calculated LTM core EBITDA of 475,642 give 9.78x, down from 10.77x at FY2025. Mechanism: the improvement comes mostly from the numerator, as 852,487 of debt was retired using equity and sale proceeds, while LTM EBITDA fell from 511,334 as hotels were sold and hotel revenue dropped. Implication: deleveraging is real but asset-sale driven, so each further hotel sale lowers both debt and EBITDA and the ratio improves only if proceeds retire debt at a higher multiple than the EBITDA sold. The hotel segment lost 272,673 in the nine months of 2026 after impairments (10-Q Q3 page:31), so the retained hotels are not yet self-supporting after impairment.

facts.text: Coverage. Evidence: LTM cash interest of 336,491 against core EBITDA of 475,642 gives 1.41x, and the fixed-rate table shows annual interest of 263,082 on the current debt (10-Q Q3 page:62). Mechanism: LTM cash interest still includes interest on notes repaid during 2026, while LTM EBITDA includes earnings of sold hotels. Implication: cover on the current debt is likely above 1.41x on a run-rate basis only if EBITDA holds, which the hotel sales make uncertain. The 2027 zero coupon notes add no cash interest but accrete at 7.50% per annum, so the cash coverage metric understates the claim growing until maturity.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The business is a two-engine REIT with different risk profiles. About a quarter of revenue is contractual rent from service-focused retail net lease properties, and the rest is hotel operating revenue where the Trust carries the operating cost and pays managers. The net lease engine is concentrated: one tenant, TravelCenters of America, accounts for 68.2% of annualized minimum rent through five master leases that expire in 2033, with a limited BP guaranty and rent coverage on those leases of 1.32x to 1.61x, against 2.17x for the whole net lease portfolio and at least 2.18x for every other top ten brand. The hotel engine is being shrunk: 112 hotels were sold in 2025, more in 2026, and 53 Sonesta managed hotels plus 17 Hyatt and seven Radisson hotels are the stated retained set.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: The Trust is externally managed. It has no employees, RMR provides all personnel, and the Chair, who is also a Managing Trustee, controls Sonesta and, through ABP Trust, the parent of RMR. That makes three related-party strands, manager, hotel operator and equity investee, which sit on both sides of fee, capital spending and asset-sale decisions. Documented behaviour in 2026 was supportive of creditors: the manager joined the equity offering, distributions were held at 0.05 per share per quarter, and the proceeds retired 1,550,000 of unsecured notes, and cash retired a 45,000 variable funding note. The same year raised the secured share of principal debt, which moves claim ranking against unsecured noteholders, although it was done through new, disclosed financings and not by amending existing notes; no non-pro-rata exchange, uptier or drop-down of existing noteholders is documented in the pack.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: In September 2025 the Trust issued zero coupon senior secured notes due 2027 with 580,155 principal at maturity, raising net proceeds of approximately 490,000. The notes accrete at 7.50% per annum, are secured by first-priority liens on the equity of subsidiaries that own 36 travel centers, and have a one-time one-year extension option (10-K FY2025 page:196: "we issued $580,155 in aggregate principal amount at maturity of zero coupon senior secured notes due 2027"). On March 6, 2026 the Issuers, special purpose bankruptcy-remote subsidiaries, issued 745,000 of Series 2026-1 net lease mortgage notes in three classes with a 5.96% weighted coupon, maturing March 2031 (10-Q Q3 page:22: "issued $745,000 in aggregate principal amount of net lease mortgage notes in three classes"). The Trust contributed 158 properties to the collateral pool and the notes are non-recourse. The proceeds and cash on hand redeemed all 700,000 of the 8.375% senior guaranteed unsecured notes due 2029 with a make whole premium of 37,128. On April 2, 2026 the Trust sold 95,833,333 common shares at 6.00 per share after the reverse split, with net proceeds of approximately 541,798, which funded the redemption of the 450,000 5.50% guaranteed notes due 2027 and, with cash on hand, the 4.95% notes due 2027 (10-Q Q3 page:48). RMR, the manager, bought 8,333,333 shares in the offering at the public price (10-Q Q3 page:29). In September 2026 the 45,000 variable funding note was repaid and terminated using existing cash (10-Q Q3 page:23).

facts.text: Revenue durability. Evidence: net lease rental income of 101,141 in Q3 2026 is 25.3% of revenue, and 68.2% of annualized minimum rent is TA. Risk mechanic: contractual rent is stable while the tenant pays, but one tenant, on leases with the lowest portfolio coverage, makes the rent stream effectively a single credit with a BP guaranty capped at 2,782,917. Credit implication: debt service from rent is supported but concentrated; a TA payment problem would affect more than two thirds of net lease rent, and the 2033 expiry sits one year after the 2032 notes mature. A counter: portfolio rent coverage is 2.17x on tenant-reported data.

Credit implication: debt service from rent is supported but concentrated; a TA payment problem would affect more than two thirds of net lease rent, and the 2033 expiry sits one year after the 2032 notes mature. A counter: portfolio rent coverage is 2.17x on tenant-reported data.

facts.text: Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: hotel operating expenses were 85.7% of hotel revenue in Q3 2026 and the hotel segment lost 52,142 after impairments. Risk mechanic: the Trust carries hotel cost and pays fee layers ahead of its own return, so a revenue decline cuts margin more than revenue. Credit implication: hotel cash flow is the swing factor for cover; improving RevPAR on retained hotels helps, but 74.7% of revenue still comes from hotels.

facts.label: Calculations
facts.text: - Hotel share of Q3 2026 revenue = 298,379 / 399,520 = 74.7% (10-Q Q3 page:3). Net lease share = 101,141 / 399,520 = 25.3%. Nine months 2026: 883,025 / 1,184,945 = 74.5%. - Hotel operating expense ratio, Q3 2026 = 255,780 / 298,379 = 85.7%; Q3 2025 = 328,358 / 377,576 = 87.0%. Nine months 2026 = 763,078 / 883,025 = 86.4%; nine months 2025 = 963,111 / 1,116,944 = 86.2%. - Hotel revenue less hotel operating expenses, Q3 2026 = 298,379 - 255,780 = 42,599; Q3 2025 = 377,576 - 328,358 = 49,218. Net lease rental income less net lease operating expenses, Q3 2026 = 101,141 - 6,389 = 94,752; Q3 2025 = 101,194 - 5,236 = 95,958 (10-Q Q3 page:3). - TA share of annualized minimum rent = 269,547 / 395,492 = 68.2%, equal to the printed 68.2% (10-Q Q3 pages:56 and 12). TA rental income in Q3 2026 of 67,834 over total rental income of 101,141 = 67.1% (10-Q Q3 pages:12 and 3). - Secured share of principal debt at December 31, 2025 = (1,580,155 senior secured + 604,654 mortgage + 45,000 variable funding note) / 5,504,809 = 2,229,809 / 5,504,809 = 40.5% (the revolver was undrawn). At September 30, 2026 = (1,580,155 + 1,347,167) / 4,652,322 = 2,927,322 / 4,652,322 = 62.9% (principal figures from the upstream debt table). - RMR purchase in the offering = 8,333,333 shares at 6.00 = 49,999,998 US dollars, about 50.0 million; as a share of the offering = 8,333,333 / 95,833,333 = 8.7% (10-Q Q3 pages:29 and 25). - Annual fixed coupon retired by the 2026 redemptions (illustrative, before amortisation) = 400,000 x 4.95% = 19,800; 450,000 x 5.50% = 24,750; 700,000 x 8.375% = 58,625; total 103,175. Annual interest on the new Series 2026-1 notes at September 30, 2026 is 44,341 (10-Q Q3 page:62). Net reduction in annual fixed coupon from these items = 103,175 - 44,341 = 58,834. This ignores the zero coupon notes' non-cash accretion and the variable funding note. - Sonesta returns to the Trust, nine months 2026 = 86,046 against 120,896 in 2025; change = (86,046 - 120,896) / 120,896 = -28.8%, reflecting fewer Sonesta hotels (10-Q Q3 page:16). - Exit hotels: 10 at September 30, 2026 with 2,304 rooms; eight sold in October 2026 with 1,509 keys leaves 2 hotels and 2,304 - 1,509 = 795 keys, equal to the 795 keys the filing says are being marketed (10-Q Q3 pages:60, 46). Retained hotels = 87 - 10 = 77, equal to the printed retained total of 77. - Distributions: FY2024 101,150 and FY2025 6,683 (10-K FY2025 page:173); nine months 2026 14,627 (10-Q Q3 page:5).

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Service Properties Trust is a highly leveraged, thinly covered REIT whose credit is improving through asset sales and 2026 equity, but it still depends on one tenant and on refinancing a revolver that expires on June 29, 2027. The strongest support is deleveraging: principal debt fell USD 852.5 million to USD 4,652.3 million, indenture tests have headroom, and net lease rent is contractual with 97.6% occupancy. The weakest point is liquidity of USD 690.1 million, nearly all an undrawn secured revolver, against USD 1,586.9 million of maturities in 2027 and 2028 and cash interest cover of 1.41x. The outcome turns on the revolver extension or refinancing, the pace and price of hotel sales, and TravelCenters of America continuing to pay rent. [CP-1 Debt and capital structure, Liquidity, Covenants; CP-1A Business and transaction view]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The most important finding is that liquidity is narrow and time-limited. At September 30, 2026 the Trust held cash of USD 40.1 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 650.0 million, together USD 690.1 million, and the revolver matures on June 29, 2027 with two six-month extensions subject to a fee and conditions; the company says it is exploring an extension or refinancing, with no replacement agreed. Fixed-rate maturities are USD 584.2 million in 2027 and USD 1,002.8 million in 2028, so USD 1,586.9 million falls due before the end of 2028 against cash of USD 40.1 million. Availability of the revolver depends on collateral performance and covenant tests whose reported ratios are not in the pack. The mechanism is that a single secured facility supplies nearly all liquidity while the largest maturities arrive within the same window, so a failed or delayed refinancing would leave asset sales and new secured debt as the only sources. (Documentary Fact for the amounts and dates; Analyst Interpretation for the conclusion.) [CP-1 Liquidity, Debt maturities, Debt and capital structure]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The third finding is that deleveraging depends on asset sales and equity that may not repeat. Debt fell by USD 852.5 million in nine months, funded by net equity proceeds of USD 541.8 million, new net lease mortgage notes, hotel and property sales and cash on hand. Each hotel sale lowers both debt and EBITDA, and further proceeds are subject to buyer demand; sales of eight hotels for USD 50.6 million closed after the quarter. The mechanism is that leverage improves only if proceeds retire debt at a higher multiple than the EBITDA sold. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the mechanism.) TravelCenters of America pays 68.2% of net lease annualized minimum rent under five master leases that expire in 2033, with rent coverage of 1.32x to 1.61x on those leases against 2.17x for the net lease portfolio, and BP Corporation North America guarantees the leases up to a cap of USD 2,782.9 million. Coverage is tenant-reported and unaudited, and the tenant's own financials are not in the pack. The leases expire one year after the 8.875% notes due 2032. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the timing link.) [CP-1A Company and operating model, Credit translations]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The fifth finding is covenant headroom in the indentures, which is adequate on the reported tests. Total debt to adjusted total assets is 53.9% against a 60% maximum, and income available for debt service to debt service is 1.83x against a 1.50x minimum, after being 58.7% and 1.59x at December 31, 2025. Holding debt constant, adjusted assets could fall by about 10.2% before the 60% test is reached, and income available for debt service could fall by about 18.0% before the 1.50x test is reached. Revolver covenants (minimum fixed charge coverage of 1.30x, collateral debt yield of 10%) have no reported figures, so their headroom is Not calculable. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the sensitivities, derived in Calculations.) [CP-1 Covenants and restrictions]

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The sixth finding is subordination. Secured principal debt of USD 2,927.3 million is 62.9% of principal debt, up from 40.5% at December 31, 2025, because secured and equity capital replaced unsecured notes; USD 1,225.0 million of unsecured notes have no guarantees. No amendment, exchange or uptier of existing notes is documented, but unsecured creditors now sit behind more secured claims, which affects loss given default for them. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the implication.) [CP-1 Debt and capital structure; CP-1A Governance and sponsor behaviour]

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Deleveraging is real and documented: principal debt fell from USD 5,504.8 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 4,652.3 million at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Calculations]. Contractual rent is a stable core: net lease properties were 97.6% occupied with USD 395.5 million of annualized minimum rent and a 7.0 year weighted remaining term, which gives revenue visibility if tenants pay (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Indenture tests have headroom on all five reported measures at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Covenants and restrictions]. All debt is fixed rate except the undrawn revolver, with an average annual coupon of 5.65% on current principal, so interest cost is not exposed to rates in the near term (Documentary Fact for the debt table; Analyst Interpretation for the exposure view) [CP-1 Calculations]. The manager bought shares in the April 2026 equity offering and distributions were held at a low level, which is documented supportive behaviour (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Retained hotels improved in the third quarter of 2026, with RevPAR up 8.3%, although the data is manager-reported and management attributes part of the gain to a weak 2025 comparison (Management Language, qualified) [CP-1A Company and operating model].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Leverage is high and cover thin at 9.78x and 1.41x on our own EBITDA proxy, because the company reports no EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation) [CP-1 Chart data]. Liquidity depends on one secured revolver that expires June 29, 2027, and maturities of USD 584.2 million in 2027 and USD 1,002.8 million in 2028 follow (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Liquidity, Debt maturities]. Hotels are 74.7% of revenue with an operating expense ratio of 85.7% in the third quarter of 2026 and a segment loss after impairments, so earnings are operationally levered and volatile (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Calculations, Company and operating model]. Tenant concentration is high: one tenant is 68.2% of net lease rent and carries the lowest rent coverage among the top ten brands (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Earnings quality is poor: nine-month 2026 net loss was USD 463.0 million including USD 270.9 million of impairments (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. The structure is secured-heavy and related-party dependent: the Trust has no employees, RMR manages it, and the Chair controls both the hotel operator Sonesta and, through ABP Trust, RMR's parent; terminating RMR without cause would require a fee based on 19 to 20 years of fees (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company profile, Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Revolver covenant ratios, tenant financials, ratings and the investor presentation are absent (Insufficient Information; the missing items are listed in Gaps and the absence is not an adverse conclusion).

### Readiness view

Overall view: READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for each of the four selected consumers (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5). No consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. No source has blocked preparation, and every source is in the effective set. A missing downstream analytical handoff is not treated as a source condition: the dependency planner sequences CP-1 and CP-1A before CP-2, and CP-2 before CP-5.

Why the view is not READY: the pack holds filed statements and notes only. The evidence chain is statement or note text, then the risk that the credit agreement, indenture covenants and any management presentation are absent, then the consequence that covenant headroom on the revolver, adjusted EBITDA-type measures and management guidance cannot be established from the pack and must be logged as gaps rather than filled.

Why the view is not CONDITIONAL: the Q3 report prints the debt note by class, the maturity table, the indenture covenant tests, liquidity and subsequent events, and the 10-K supplies the audited annual base. The method of each consumer can run on those pages with bounded gaps.

Strongest contrary evidence: the committed revolving facility is the line the filing relies on for cash needs, and the filing says "We are currently exploring our options to extend or refinance our secured revolving credit facility." (Q3 10-Q, page:47). Its covenants and borrowing-base style conditions sit in a credit agreement that is not in the pack, so the consumers that size liquidity must carry that as a limitation.
### Per-source assessment
#### Annual report, FY2025

The 10-K is the audited base. The auditor opinion begins "We have audited the accompanying consolidated balance sheets of Service Properties Trust" (10-K, page:167). The cover gives the share count as "Number of the registrant’s common shares outstanding as of February 23, 2026: 168,061,029." (10-K, page:2). The balance sheet gives "168,070,129 and 166,636,537 shares issued and outstanding" (10-K, page:171). These are before the July 2026 reverse split. Schedule III is headed "(dollars in millions)" (10-K, page:213) while the notes to it say "NOTES TO SCHEDULE III December 31, 2025 (dollars in thousands)" (10-K, page:218). The unit label differs inside the same schedule and must be checked before any Schedule III figure is used.
#### Quarterly reports, Q1 to Q3 2026

All three are unaudited condensed statements and carry a three-month column (Q2 and Q3 also a year-to-date column). Q1 reports "168,054,570 and 168,070,129 shares issued and outstanding" (Q1 10-Q, page:2), which is unadjusted. Q2 reports "129,527,433 and 33,614,025 shares issued and outstanding" (Q2 10-Q, page:2), which is adjusted for the split. The Q3 10-Q states that share information is "retroactively adjusted for the 1-for-5 reverse share split" (Q3 10-Q, page:8) and its equity statement restates the March 31, 2026 balance as 33,610,914 shares (Q3 10-Q, page:3). The Q1 10-Q and the 10-K therefore cannot be combined with Q2 or Q3 share data without a split adjustment.

The Q3 10-Q carries the full statement set. Balance sheet: "Cash and cash equivalents 40,118 346,813" for September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025 (page:2). Income statement: "Net loss (87,940) (46,945) (462,956) (201,539)" for the three and nine months of 2026 and 2025 (page:3). Cash flow: "Cash paid for interest $ 196,080 $ 239,155" for the nine months (page:5). Segment note: "Segment profit (loss) 36,414 (52,142) (15,728) 47,206 6,909 54,115" for the three months, net lease then hotels then total (page:31). All amounts are in USD thousands.
#### Debt, liquidity and covenants evidence in the Q3 10-Q

Debt note: "Our principal debt obligations at September 30, 2026 were: (1) $1,725,000 aggregate outstanding principal amount of senior unsecured notes" (page:20), with senior secured notes and net lease mortgage notes also stated there. The mortgage note table closes with "Total / weighted average $ 1,347,167 5.80%" (page:22). A per-instrument carrying value and fair value table is on page:33. The maturity table totals "$ 4,652,322" (page:49). Revolver: "we had no amounts outstanding under our revolving credit facility and $650,000 available for borrowing" (page:20), and "The maturity date of our revolving credit facility is June 29, 2027" (page:20). The indenture tests are printed, for example "Total debt / adjusted total assets 53.9% Maximum of 60%" and "Consolidated income available for debt service / debt service 1.83x Minimum of 1.50x" (page:51). The guarantee perimeter is stated: "Our $1,225,000 of senior unsecured notes do not have the benefit of any guarantees." (page:53).

Prior-quarter revolver status for the quarter bridge: the Q2 10-Q reports "$25,000 of borrowings outstanding under our $650,000 revolving credit facility" (Q2 10-Q, page:49), and the Q1 10-Q reports "we had no amounts outstanding under our revolving credit facility and $650,000 available for borrowing" (Q1 10-Q, page:17).

Business facts: "Our net lease properties generated rent coverage of 2.17x and 2.04x as of September 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively." (page:43). Subsequent events through the filing are stated, for example "From October 1, 2026 through November 2, 2026, we sold one net lease property" (page:46). The cover gives "Number of registrant’s common shares of beneficial interest, $.01 par value per share, outstanding as of November 2, 2026: 129,813,906." (page:1).
#### Earnings-release exhibits

The three EX-99.1 files are one-page announcements. Each says the results "can be found at the Quarterly Results section of SVC’s website" (Q3 release, page:1; the same wording is on page:1 of the Q1 and Q2 releases). They contain no income statement, balance sheet, adjusted measure, reconciliation or guidance. The Q3 release adds "SVC also posted an updated investor presentation to its website." (page:1) but the presentation is not in the pack, so its content cannot be used and nothing in this review relies on it. The releases do give portfolio counts, for example "87 hotels with approximately 20,000 guest rooms" at September 30, 2026 (Q3 release, page:1). They are management statements and are subordinate to the filed 10-Q, which reports 87 hotels at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q, page:7).
#### Conflicts

No conflict between sources was found in the items checked. The one difference noted is a unit label, not a conflicting figure: the Schedule III heading in millions against its notes in thousands (10-K, page:213 and page:218). Its downstream effect falls on any consumer that uses Schedule III property data.
#### Version relationships

The three 10-Qs are separate active periodic reports for consecutive quarters, and the 10-K is the annual report. None supersedes another. The Q3 10-Q supersedes the earlier 10-Qs only for facts stated as of September 30, 2026. Prior-period comparatives inside later filings are retained as stated there; this module does not rule which version controls a given fact.
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | View | Evidence located | Limitations carried |

| CP-1 (financial and credit data) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Statements, debt note by class, maturity table, indenture tests, liquidity and cash flow in the Q3 10-Q; audited base in the 10-K | Revolver covenant levels not supplied; no adjusted EBITDA-type measure outside filings; split-unadjusted share data in the 10-K and Q1 10-Q; Schedule III unit label |

| CP-1A (business and transaction context) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Business description and operating model in the 10-K; tenant and manager concentration, segment note, related-party notes in the Q3 10-Q | No investor presentation; ownership and sponsor fields in the context are blank; management narrative limited to filing text |
| CP-2 (credit synthesis) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Depends on CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, which the planner sequences | Inherits every CP-1 and CP-1A limitation; no ratings in the context |

| CP-5 (evidence trace) | READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS | Depends on settled upstream modules and the pinned pack | Inherits upstream limitations; cannot test claims that rest on documents outside the pack |
### Model objective coverage

For the HTML Model objective the pack holds: discrete three-month columns for each of Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 and the 2025 comparatives; year-to-date columns in the Q2 and Q3 reports; FY2025 and FY2024 annual statements in the 10-K; a segment note for net lease and hotels; debt by class with carrying and fair values; and cash paid for interest and income taxes (Q3 10-Q, page:5 and the supplemental table after it). Source evidence is sufficient for these. The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. This module does not assert normalised quarters, reconciliation or downstream input acceptance. A last-twelve-month view and Q4 2025 are not printed as such and would have to be derived downstream from filed columns; that derivation is not performed here.
## Calculations

None. CP-0 does not normalise, reconcile or calculate figures. Every amount quoted above is copied as printed, in USD thousands unless the text states a count, a ratio or a percentage. The following were deliberately not derived: last-twelve-month figures, Q4 2025, net debt, leverage ratios, liquidity totals and covenant headroom. Each is Not calculable in this module because it is a downstream analytical step, not because an input is missing.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected consumers | Why it matters | Remediation |

| Credit agreement for the $650,000 secured revolver is not in the pack. Financial covenant levels and borrowing conditions are described only in general terms (Q3 10-Q, page:20 and page:21). | High | CP-1, CP-2, CP-5 | Covenant headroom and drawing conditions on the revolver, which matures June 29, 2027, cannot be tested. | Obtain the credit agreement and its amendments, or log headroom as Not calculable. |

| Indentures and supplements for the senior secured and unsecured notes are not in the pack. Only the summary tests on page:51 of the Q3 10-Q are available. | Medium | CP-1, CP-2 | Definitions of adjusted total assets and income available for debt service cannot be checked. | Obtain the indentures if definitions are needed; otherwise cite the printed tests as issuer-reported. |

| Earnings releases carry no figures, adjusted measures or guidance; the Q3 investor presentation is not in the pack. | Medium | CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 | No management bridge or guidance; slides cannot be inspected from this pack. | Obtain the website results document and presentation if management claims are wanted. |

| Share data is unadjusted for the 1-for-5 reverse split in the 10-K and the Q1 10-Q, and adjusted in the Q2 and Q3 10-Qs. | Medium | CP-1 | Per-share and share-count comparisons across filings are not like for like. | Use split-adjusted amounts from the Q3 10-Q for 2025 and 2026 comparisons, or restate explicitly. |

| Schedule III heading "(dollars in millions)" against notes "(dollars in thousands)" (10-K, page:213 and page:218). | Low | CP-1 | Wrong scale if a Schedule III figure is used. | Check the scale against the balance sheet before use. |

| Context leaves ratings, market capitalisation, net debt, peers and deal terms blank. | Low | CP-2 | No external ratings or market-based cross-check is available. Blank is not zero. | Supply ratings and market data if wanted; otherwise treat as Not supplied. |

| Original HTML tables, charts and images were not inspected; only extracted text was reviewed. This is a text-extraction review, not a fidelity review. | Low | All | Table alignment errors in the extraction are possible. | Check key figures against the statements when used. |

| The dollar scale of the 10-K and 10-Qs is stated in thousands, and the reporting currency of the context is USD. No other currency or period basis was found in the sources. | Low | All | None identified. | None required. |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-1 (financial and credit data) and CP-1A (business and transaction context), then CP-2 and CP-5 in dependency order. All four are READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS. CP-1 should take the Q3 10-Q as the primary source for the September 30, 2026 position and the 10-K for the audited FY2025 base, apply the split adjustment where share data is compared, and record the revolver covenant levels as Not supplied. Do not use the investor presentation referred to in the Q3 release as evidence, because it is not in the pack.

spans.text: ## Request

Module CP-1, financial base and credit metrics, for Service Properties Trust (SVC, issuer id svc), as of 2026-11-05 (cutoff 2026-11-05), pathway credit_snapshot, reporting currency USD. The module extracts the reported financial base from the pinned filings, calculates leverage, interest cover, liquidity and maturity data with every input shown, and carries the source-readiness limitations from the upstream handoff.

Perimeter: the registrant, Service Properties Trust, and its consolidated subsidiaries, including consolidated taxable REIT subsidiaries. No separate borrower, parent or guarantor statements exist in the sources. The issuer of the senior notes is the Trust itself; the net lease mortgage notes are issued by bankruptcy-remote subsidiaries that are consolidated.

Units and periods: the filings print dollars in thousands. Statement tables below are in USD thousands as printed. The four chart tables convert to US$m by dividing by 1,000, which is a change of scale only. Periods follow the filings: FY2024 and FY2025 (years ended December 31), Q1 2026, Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 (three months ended March 31, June 30 and September 30, 2026), nine months 2026 and nine months 2025 (ended September 30), and last twelve months (LTM) periods derived as FY2025 plus the 2026 year-to-date period less the 2025 year-to-date period. The context labels q3-2026 and fy-2025 match these periods.

### Short names and locators
10-K FY2025, 10-Q Q1, 10-Q Q2 and 10-Q Q3 name the four filings. A locator `page:N` is the chunk number in the pinned extraction file, not the printed page.
### Correction to the upstream handoff

CP-0 listed the revolver covenant levels as not supplied and said the credit agreement terms are described only in general terms. The 10-K FY2025 does print two revolver covenant terms: "reduce the minimum fixed charge coverage ratio covenant from 1.50x to 1.30x effective with respect to the fourth quarter of 2024" and "change the required collateral property debt yield to 10%" (10-K FY2025, page:195). What remains unsupplied is the issuer's reported figure for either test at any date, and the credit agreement itself, so revolver headroom is still Not calculable. The CP-0 statement was right for the 10-Q filings and incomplete for the 10-K. CP-0 cannot be edited, so this answer is the correction.
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Debt fell from 5,504,809 to 4,652,322 through 2026, but leverage on a calculated last-twelve-month core EBITDA of 475,642 is still 9.78x gross and 9.70x net, and cash interest cover is 1.41x. | Medium | The company reports no EBITDA, and the credit agreement ratios and headroom are not supplied. Core EBITDA is our own definition and includes sold hotels. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Liquidity at September 30, 2026 is cash of 40,118 plus an undrawn revolver of 650,000, but the revolver matures June 29, 2027 and an extension or refinancing is being explored. | Almost all liquidity is one secured facility that expires within nine months, so the refinancing outcome drives near-term risk. | High |

| Fixed-rate debt maturities are 584,150 in 2027 and 1,002,775 in 2028, against cash of 40,118. | Repayment depends on asset sales, new secured debt or equity, which the company has used heavily in 2026. | High |

| The senior notes tests at September 30, 2026 are 53.9% total debt to adjusted assets against a 60% maximum, and 1.83x debt service cover against a 1.50x minimum. | Headroom improved from December 31, 2025 (58.7% and 1.59x) after debt repayment and equity issuance, but debt service cover is the tighter test. | High |

| Nine-month 2026 net loss was 462,956, including impairments of 270,883, and hotel revenue fell with hotel sales. | Earnings quality is weak and the hotel base keeps shrinking, so past EBITDA overstates what the retained portfolio earns. | Medium |
### Financial base view

The reported financial base is complete enough for the requested use, with limits. Four filings give full statements, a debt note by class, a maturity table, the senior notes indenture tests, revolver availability and subsequent events through November 2, 2026. The company prints no EBITDA, so the leverage and cover charts use a core EBITDA defined and calculated here from statement lines: total revenues less hotel operating expenses, net lease operating expenses, general and administrative expenses and transaction related costs. It excludes depreciation, impairments, gains and losses on sales, early extinguishment losses and equity in losses of an investee. It is not an issuer figure and not a covenant measure.

On that basis the trust is highly levered and thinly covered but de-risked by a year of debt reduction. Principal debt fell by 852,487 from December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026, funded by net equity proceeds of 541,798, new net lease mortgage notes, asset sales and cash on hand. Gross leverage on LTM core EBITDA moved from 10.77x at FY2025 to 9.78x at the third quarter of 2026, and cash interest cover from 1.35x to 1.41x. Both are weak, and the LTM EBITDA still includes earnings of hotels that have since been sold, so forward leverage on the retained portfolio is likely worse than the LTM figure shows; that last point is analyst inference, not a reported number. Liquidity is thin in cash and rests on a single undrawn secured revolver that matures within nine months. The balance sheet is secured-heavy: secured principal of 2,927,322 is 63% of principal debt, a share calculated in the Calculations section.

Limits on this view: no issuer EBITDA, no credit agreement ratios or headroom, share data that mixes split-adjusted and unadjusted bases across filings, unaudited interim statements, and hotel operating data that the company states it has not verified.

The 1-for-5 reverse share split took effect after the close of trading on July 6, 2026.
- Revolver: no draw at September 30, 2026; the company says "We are currently exploring our options to extend or refinance our secured revolving credit facility" (10-Q Q3 page:47).

- Dispositions: 32 properties sold in the nine months for 88,159; six hotels sold in Q3 for 66,100 (10-Q Q3 page:10). Held for sale at September 30, 2026: nine hotels with 1,809 keys and six net lease properties (10-Q Q3 page:10).

- Subsequent events through November 2, 2026 (stated in the Q3 10-Q, dated before the cutoff): sale of eight hotels with 1,509 keys for 50,600 and one net lease property for 295; acquisition of four net lease properties for 8,314; a pending sale of one net lease property for 655 that is subject to conditions (10-Q Q3 pages:11 and 46). A regular distribution of $0.05 per share, about 6,491, was declared October 8, 2026 and is to be paid on or about November 12, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:47).

- The announcement dated November 4, 2026 reports 87 hotels and 740 net lease properties at September 30, 2026 and refers to results and a presentation on the company website that are not in the pack.
### Interpretation: evidence, mechanism and credit implication

Leverage. Evidence: principal debt of 4,652,322 and calculated LTM core EBITDA of 475,642 give 9.78x, down from 10.77x at FY2025. Mechanism: the improvement comes mostly from the numerator, as 852,487 of debt was retired using equity and sale proceeds, while LTM EBITDA fell from 511,334 as hotels were sold and hotel revenue dropped. Implication: deleveraging is real but asset-sale driven, so each further hotel sale lowers both debt and EBITDA and the ratio improves only if proceeds retire debt at a higher multiple than the EBITDA sold. The hotel segment lost 272,673 in the nine months of 2026 after impairments (10-Q Q3 page:31), so the retained hotels are not yet self-supporting after impairment.

Coverage. Evidence: LTM cash interest of 336,491 against core EBITDA of 475,642 gives 1.41x, and the fixed-rate table shows annual interest of 263,082 on the current debt (10-Q Q3 page:62). Mechanism: LTM cash interest still includes interest on notes repaid during 2026, while LTM EBITDA includes earnings of sold hotels. Implication: cover on the current debt is likely above 1.41x on a run-rate basis only if EBITDA holds, which the hotel sales make uncertain. The 2027 zero coupon notes add no cash interest but accrete at 7.50% per annum, so the cash coverage metric understates the claim growing until maturity.

Liquidity and refinancing. Evidence: cash of 40,118, an undrawn 650,000 revolver maturing June 29, 2027, maturities of 584,150 in 2027 and 1,002,775 in 2028, and the stated search for a revolver extension or refinancing. Mechanism: the revolver is secured on 55 properties and its availability depends on collateral performance, value and covenants, including a fixed charge coverage minimum of 1.30x that the pack does not report against. Implication: the 2027 wall (revolver expiry and the zero coupon notes) is the near-term pressure point. The two six-month extension options require a fee and a 1.50x fixed charge coverage ratio for the first extension, a test the pack gives no figure for.

Structure. Evidence: secured principal (senior secured notes plus mortgage notes) of 2,927,322 against unsecured notes of 1,725,000, of which 1,225,000 is not guaranteed. Mechanism: unsecured and unguaranteed creditors sit behind secured claims on the best assets and behind subsidiary-level claims. Implication: recovery for the 1,225,000 of unguaranteed unsecured notes depends on residual value after secured claims; the indenture test of unencumbered assets to unsecured debt at 273.2% shows asset cover on the company's definition but is not a recovery estimate.
## Calculations
All inputs are in USD thousands as printed and locators are page chunks. Rounding is to two decimals for ratios.
### Core EBITDA

Definition: total revenues less hotel operating expenses, less net lease operating expenses, less general and administrative, less transaction related costs. Equivalent to net loss plus income tax plus interest expense plus depreciation and amortization less interest income plus impairment plus loss on sales plus early extinguishment loss plus equity in losses of an investee. The company reports no EBITDA, so this is an analyst-defined proxy.

Sum of the 2027 maturities and cash on hand: 584,150 - 40,118 = 544,032 to be funded by other sources, before the revolver's own June 29, 2027 expiry.
### Cash flow and LTM operating lines

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Service Properties Trust is an externally managed REIT whose rent comes largely from one tenant, while its hotels, run mostly by an affiliated operator, are being sold. 2026 deleveraging was funded by equity and secured debt. | Medium | No investor presentation, rating or tenant financials are in the pack, and ownership beyond two holders near 6% is not disclosed. |

| TravelCenters of America pays 68.2% of annualized minimum rent under five leases that expire in 2033, backed by a capped guaranty from BP Corporation North America. | Rent durability rests on one tenant and one guarantor, and the leases expire one year after the 2032 notes mature. | High |

### Business and transaction view

The business is a two-engine REIT with different risk profiles. About a quarter of revenue is contractual rent from service-focused retail net lease properties, and the rest is hotel operating revenue where the Trust carries the operating cost and pays managers. The net lease engine is concentrated: one tenant, TravelCenters of America, accounts for 68.2% of annualized minimum rent through five master leases that expire in 2033, with a limited BP guaranty and rent coverage on those leases of 1.32x to 1.61x, against 2.17x for the whole net lease portfolio and at least 2.18x for every other top ten brand. The hotel engine is being shrunk: 112 hotels were sold in 2025, more in 2026, and 53 Sonesta managed hotels plus 17 Hyatt and seven Radisson hotels are the stated retained set.

The Trust is externally managed. It has no employees, RMR provides all personnel, and the Chair, who is also a Managing Trustee, controls Sonesta and, through ABP Trust, the parent of RMR. That makes three related-party strands, manager, hotel operator and equity investee, which sit on both sides of fee, capital spending and asset-sale decisions. Documented behaviour in 2026 was supportive of creditors: the manager joined the equity offering, distributions were held at 0.05 per share per quarter, and the proceeds retired 1,550,000 of unsecured notes, and cash retired a 45,000 variable funding note. The same year raised the secured share of principal debt, which moves claim ranking against unsecured noteholders, although it was done through new, disclosed financings and not by amending existing notes; no non-pro-rata exchange, uptier or drop-down of existing noteholders is documented in the pack.

Evidence quality is high for filed facts and low-to-medium for manager-reported hotel statistics and tenant-reported rent coverage, which the company states it does not verify. The investor presentation referenced in the November 4, 2026 announcement is not in the pack, so management language beyond the filings is unavailable.

These are subsequent events and are not folded into September 30, 2026 figures. Eight of the ten exit hotels have therefore been sold and two remain for sale, which matches the 795 keys the filing says it is marketing; the retained set of 77 hotels is the earnings base going forward.

Related-party transaction in Q3 2026: in connection with a hotel sale, Sonesta waived an 11,035 termination fee in exchange for an extension of the management agreement for the remaining Sonesta retained hotels through June 30, 2043, and the Trust recorded the fee as an impairment loss (10-Q Q3 page:16). Use of proceeds is therefore stated and verifiable: debt retirement. No debt-funded distribution, dividend recapitalisation or asset drop-down to unrestricted subsidiaries is documented in the pack.

### Credit translations

Revenue durability. Evidence: net lease rental income of 101,141 in Q3 2026 is 25.3% of revenue, and 68.2% of annualized minimum rent is TA. Risk mechanic: contractual rent is stable while the tenant pays, but one tenant, on leases with the lowest portfolio coverage, makes the rent stream effectively a single credit with a BP guaranty capped at 2,782,917. Credit implication: debt service from rent is supported but concentrated; a TA payment problem would affect more than two thirds of net lease rent, and the 2033 expiry sits one year after the 2032 notes mature. A counter: portfolio rent coverage is 2.17x on tenant-reported data.

Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: hotel operating expenses were 85.7% of hotel revenue in Q3 2026 and the hotel segment lost 52,142 after impairments. Risk mechanic: the Trust carries hotel cost and pays fee layers ahead of its own return, so a revenue decline cuts margin more than revenue. Credit implication: hotel cash flow is the swing factor for cover; improving RevPAR on retained hotels helps, but 74.7% of revenue still comes from hotels.

Concentration and related-party risk. Evidence: Sonesta manages 62 hotels, about 39.9% of total historical real estate investments, and is controlled by the Chair; RMR runs the Trust with no employees. Risk mechanic: fees, capital spending and sale decisions are negotiated between related parties. Credit implication: monitoring of related-party flows is a standing requirement; the Q3 fee waiver for a longer term shows the trade-offs.

Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor exists, RMR bought shares in the offering, distributions were held at a low level. Risk mechanic: manager fees are asset and return based, not leverage based. Credit implication: alignment is moderate; support is modest in size and not a commitment.

Key uncertainties. The June 29, 2027 revolver expiry, the 2027 and 2028 maturities, the TA lease profile, and missing credit agreement ratios dominate. Counter-evidence: the equity raise and 2026 redemptions reduced principal debt to 4,652,322.

## Calculations
Inputs are USD thousands as printed; locators are page chunks.

- Hotel revenue less hotel operating expenses, Q3 2026 = 298,379 - 255,780 = 42,599; Q3 2025 = 377,576 - 328,358 = 49,218. Net lease rental income less net lease operating expenses, Q3 2026 = 101,141 - 6,389 = 94,752; Q3 2025 = 101,194 - 5,236 = 95,958 (10-Q Q3 page:3).

- TA share of annualized minimum rent = 269,547 / 395,492 = 68.2%, equal to the printed 68.2% (10-Q Q3 pages:56 and 12). TA rental income in Q3 2026 of 67,834 over total rental income of 101,141 = 67.1% (10-Q Q3 pages:12 and 3).

- Secured share of principal debt at December 31, 2025 = (1,580,155 senior secured + 604,654 mortgage + 45,000 variable funding note) / 5,504,809 = 2,229,809 / 5,504,809 = 40.5% (the revolver was undrawn). At September 30, 2026 = (1,580,155 + 1,347,167) / 4,652,322 = 2,927,322 / 4,652,322 = 62.9% (principal figures from the upstream debt table).
- RMR purchase in the offering = 8,333,333 shares at 6.00 = 49,999,998 US dollars, about 50.0 million; as a share of the offering = 8,333,333 / 95,833,333 = 8.7% (10-Q Q3 pages:29 and 25).

- Annual fixed coupon retired by the 2026 redemptions (illustrative, before amortisation) = 400,000 x 4.95% = 19,800; 450,000 x 5.50% = 24,750; 700,000 x 8.375% = 58,625; total 103,175. Annual interest on the new Series 2026-1 notes at September 30, 2026 is 44,341 (10-Q Q3 page:62). Net reduction in annual fixed coupon from these items = 103,175 - 44,341 = 58,834. This ignores the zero coupon notes' non-cash accretion and the variable funding note.
- Sonesta returns to the Trust, nine months 2026 = 86,046 against 120,896 in 2025; change = (86,046 - 120,896) / 120,896 = -28.8%, reflecting fewer Sonesta hotels (10-Q Q3 page:16).

- Exit hotels: 10 at September 30, 2026 with 2,304 rooms; eight sold in October 2026 with 1,509 keys leaves 2 hotels and 2,304 - 1,509 = 795 keys, equal to the 795 keys the filing says are being marketed (10-Q Q3 pages:60, 46). Retained hotels = 87 - 10 = 77, equal to the printed retained total of 77.
- Distributions: FY2024 101,150 and FY2025 6,683 (10-K FY2025 page:173); nine months 2026 14,627 (10-Q Q3 page:5).

### Credit view

Service Properties Trust is a highly leveraged, thinly covered REIT whose credit is improving through asset sales and 2026 equity, but it still depends on one tenant and on refinancing a revolver that expires on June 29, 2027. The strongest support is deleveraging: principal debt fell USD 852.5 million to USD 4,652.3 million, indenture tests have headroom, and net lease rent is contractual with 97.6% occupancy. The weakest point is liquidity of USD 690.1 million, nearly all an undrawn secured revolver, against USD 1,586.9 million of maturities in 2027 and 2028 and cash interest cover of 1.41x. The outcome turns on the revolver extension or refinancing, the pace and price of hotel sales, and TravelCenters of America continuing to pay rent. [CP-1 Debt and capital structure, Liquidity, Covenants; CP-1A Business and transaction view]
### Credit assessment
| Item | Statement | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Weak but improving: high leverage and thin cover offset by 2026 deleveraging, covenant headroom and contractual rent; refinancing risk is the swing factor | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 leverage, interest cover, liquidity and covenant tables; CP-1A Company and operating model rows on tenant concentration, hotel model and strategy; CP-1A Transaction summary |

| Confidence limit | Confidence is below High because leverage rests on an analyst-defined EBITDA proxy, revolver covenant headroom is Not calculable, and CP-1A judged this module READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS while recording unverified tenant and manager data | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 Gaps; CP-1A Gaps; CP-1A Consumer read-through |
### Thesis

Service Properties Trust is a deleveraging, hotel-to-net-lease transition credit whose debt service is supported by concentrated contractual rent but whose near-term outcome depends on refinancing the 2027 revolver and executing hotel sales on acceptable terms. (Analyst Interpretation; basis: CP-1 Financial base view and CP-1A Business and transaction view.)
### Key findings

The most important finding is that liquidity is narrow and time-limited. At September 30, 2026 the Trust held cash of USD 40.1 million and an undrawn revolver of USD 650.0 million, together USD 690.1 million, and the revolver matures on June 29, 2027 with two six-month extensions subject to a fee and conditions; the company says it is exploring an extension or refinancing, with no replacement agreed. Fixed-rate maturities are USD 584.2 million in 2027 and USD 1,002.8 million in 2028, so USD 1,586.9 million falls due before the end of 2028 against cash of USD 40.1 million. Availability of the revolver depends on collateral performance and covenant tests whose reported ratios are not in the pack. The mechanism is that a single secured facility supplies nearly all liquidity while the largest maturities arrive within the same window, so a failed or delayed refinancing would leave asset sales and new secured debt as the only sources. (Documentary Fact for the amounts and dates; Analyst Interpretation for the conclusion.) [CP-1 Liquidity, Debt maturities, Debt and capital structure]

The second finding is that leverage and cover are weak even after 2026 deleveraging. Principal debt of USD 4,652.3 million is 9.78x calculated last-twelve-month core EBITDA of USD 475.6 million (9.70x net of USD 40.1 million cash), down from 10.77x at FY2025, and core EBITDA covers last-twelve-month cash interest 1.41x, up from 1.35x. The Trust has a net loss of USD 463.7 million over the last twelve months, including USD 271.0 million of impairments, and operating cash flow less real estate improvements was negative USD 73.0 million. The EBITDA proxy includes earnings of hotels that have since been sold, so forward leverage on the retained portfolio is likely higher than shown. (Documentary Fact for reported amounts; Analyst Interpretation for the proxy and its direction, which is our inference and not a reported number.) [CP-1 Chart data, Financials and credit metrics, Calculations]

The third finding is that deleveraging depends on asset sales and equity that may not repeat. Debt fell by USD 852.5 million in nine months, funded by net equity proceeds of USD 541.8 million, new net lease mortgage notes, hotel and property sales and cash on hand. Each hotel sale lowers both debt and EBITDA, and further proceeds are subject to buyer demand; sales of eight hotels for USD 50.6 million closed after the quarter. The mechanism is that leverage improves only if proceeds retire debt at a higher multiple than the EBITDA sold. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the mechanism.) [CP-1 Latest quarter and events; CP-1A Transaction summary]

The fourth finding is rent concentration. TravelCenters of America pays 68.2% of net lease annualized minimum rent under five master leases that expire in 2033, with rent coverage of 1.32x to 1.61x on those leases against 2.17x for the net lease portfolio, and BP Corporation North America guarantees the leases up to a cap of USD 2,782.9 million. Coverage is tenant-reported and unaudited, and the tenant's own financials are not in the pack. The leases expire one year after the 8.875% notes due 2032. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the timing link.) [CP-1A Company and operating model, Credit translations]

The fifth finding is covenant headroom in the indentures, which is adequate on the reported tests. Total debt to adjusted total assets is 53.9% against a 60% maximum, and income available for debt service to debt service is 1.83x against a 1.50x minimum, after being 58.7% and 1.59x at December 31, 2025. Holding debt constant, adjusted assets could fall by about 10.2% before the 60% test is reached, and income available for debt service could fall by about 18.0% before the 1.50x test is reached. Revolver covenants (minimum fixed charge coverage of 1.30x, collateral debt yield of 10%) have no reported figures, so their headroom is Not calculable. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the sensitivities, derived in Calculations.) [CP-1 Covenants and restrictions]

The sixth finding is subordination. Secured principal debt of USD 2,927.3 million is 62.9% of principal debt, up from 40.5% at December 31, 2025, because secured and equity capital replaced unsecured notes; USD 1,225.0 million of unsecured notes have no guarantees. No amendment, exchange or uptier of existing notes is documented, but unsecured creditors now sit behind more secured claims, which affects loss given default for them. (Documentary Fact; Analyst Interpretation for the implication.) [CP-1 Debt and capital structure; CP-1A Governance and sponsor behaviour]
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Deleveraging is real and documented: principal debt fell from USD 5,504.8 million at December 31, 2025 to USD 4,652.3 million at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Calculations]. Contractual rent is a stable core: net lease properties were 97.6% occupied with USD 395.5 million of annualized minimum rent and a 7.0 year weighted remaining term, which gives revenue visibility if tenants pay (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Indenture tests have headroom on all five reported measures at September 30, 2026 (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Covenants and restrictions]. All debt is fixed rate except the undrawn revolver, with an average annual coupon of 5.65% on current principal, so interest cost is not exposed to rates in the near term (Documentary Fact for the debt table; Analyst Interpretation for the exposure view) [CP-1 Calculations]. The manager bought shares in the April 2026 equity offering and distributions were held at a low level, which is documented supportive behaviour (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Retained hotels improved in the third quarter of 2026, with RevPAR up 8.3%, although the data is manager-reported and management attributes part of the gain to a weak 2025 comparison (Management Language, qualified) [CP-1A Company and operating model].

Weaknesses. Leverage is high and cover thin at 9.78x and 1.41x on our own EBITDA proxy, because the company reports no EBITDA (Analyst Interpretation) [CP-1 Chart data]. Liquidity depends on one secured revolver that expires June 29, 2027, and maturities of USD 584.2 million in 2027 and USD 1,002.8 million in 2028 follow (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Liquidity, Debt maturities]. Hotels are 74.7% of revenue with an operating expense ratio of 85.7% in the third quarter of 2026 and a segment loss after impairments, so earnings are operationally levered and volatile (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Calculations, Company and operating model]. Tenant concentration is high: one tenant is 68.2% of net lease rent and carries the lowest rent coverage among the top ten brands (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company and operating model]. Earnings quality is poor: nine-month 2026 net loss was USD 463.0 million including USD 270.9 million of impairments (Documentary Fact) [CP-1 Financials and credit metrics]. The structure is secured-heavy and related-party dependent: the Trust has no employees, RMR manages it, and the Chair controls both the hotel operator Sonesta and, through ABP Trust, RMR's parent; terminating RMR without cause would require a fee based on 19 to 20 years of fees (Documentary Fact) [CP-1A Company profile, Governance and sponsor behaviour]. Revolver covenant ratios, tenant financials, ratings and the investor presentation are absent (Insufficient Information; the missing items are listed in Gaps and the absence is not an adverse conclusion).
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Revolver expiry and 2027 to 2028 maturities | One secured facility is nearly all liquidity and expires June 29, 2027; extension needs a fee and conditions, and availability depends on collateral and covenants | A failed refinancing leaves asset sales and new secured debt as the only sources, raising default and refinancing risk | Critical | CP-1 Liquidity, Debt maturities, Covenants |

| High leverage and thin cover | Debt is 9.78x core EBITDA and cash interest cover 1.41x, with the EBITDA proxy including sold hotels | Little cushion if hotel earnings or rent weaken; deleveraging must continue | Material | CP-1 Chart data, Calculations |

| Tenant concentration | One tenant is 68.2% of net lease rent, with lowest rent coverage and a capped guaranty; leases expire 2033 | Tenant stress would cut most net lease rent and the 2032 notes mature one year before expiry | Material | CP-1A Company and operating model |

| Hotel earnings and disposal execution | Hotel costs and fee layers are borne by the Trust; sales depend on buyers and impair assets | Falling EBITDA and impairments can offset debt paydown | Material | CP-1A Company and operating model; CP-1 Latest quarter |

| Subordination of unsecured creditors | Secured share of principal debt rose from 40.5% to 62.9%; USD 1,225.0 million of unsecured notes are unguaranteed | Higher loss given default exposure for unsecured notes | Material | CP-1 Debt and capital structure; CP-1A Governance |

| Related-party dependence | RMR manages the Trust with no employees; Sonesta manages 62 hotels and is controlled by the Chair; fees and capital spending are negotiated between related parties | Weak creditor control over operating decisions and costly manager exit | Minor | CP-1A Company profile, Governance and sponsor behaviour |
## Calculations
New calculations in this answer:

- Maturities to the end of 2028 = 584,150 + 1,002,775 = 1,586,925 (USD 1,586.9 million). Less cash of 40,118 = 1,546,807 to be funded from other sources (USD 1,546.8 million), before the 650,000 revolver expiry. Liquidity was 690,118 = 40,118 + 650,000.

- Adjusted total assets cushion on the total debt test: debt of 4,652,322 at the 60% limit supports adjusted total assets of 4,652,322 / 0.60 = 7,753,870. Reported adjusted total assets were 8,631,686, so the cushion is 8,631,686 - 7,753,870 = 877,816, which is 877,816 / 8,631,686 = 10.2%. For the secured test, secured debt of 2,927,322 at the 40% limit supports 2,927,322 / 0.40 = 7,318,305, a cushion of 15.2%. The total debt test binds first.
- Income available for debt service cushion: (1.83x - 1.50x) / 1.83x = 18.0%. This holds debt service constant and uses the indenture definition, not our EBITDA proxy.

- Run-rate cover on current fixed debt, illustrative: core EBITDA of 475,642 / annual fixed-rate interest of 263,082 = 1.81x. It is not used in the findings because core EBITDA includes sold hotels and the interest figure excludes accretion on the zero coupon notes.
- Equity to total assets at September 30, 2026 = 712,749 / 5,720,456 = 12.5%.

Figures taken unchanged from the upstream handoffs: gross leverage 9.78x and 10.77x, net leverage 9.70x, cash interest cover 1.41x and 1.35x, secured share 62.9% and 40.5%, hotel share of revenue 74.7%, hotel operating expense ratio 85.7%, TravelCenters of America share of rent 68.2%, average coupon 5.65%, and the covenant tests.
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Revolver covenant ratios (fixed charge coverage minimum of 1.30x, collateral debt yield of 10%) and the credit agreement are not reported or supplied; headroom is Not calculable (CP-1). | The revolver is nearly all liquidity and its availability is conditional. | Liquidity, refinancing assessment | High | Obtain the credit agreement and compliance certificates |

| The company reports no EBITDA; core EBITDA is an analyst proxy that includes sold hotels (CP-1). | Leverage and cover on the retained portfolio are uncertain, likely worse than shown. | Leverage and cover findings | High | Obtain pro forma retained-asset earnings if published |

| Tenant financial statements, guaranty terms beyond the cap, and tenant-reported coverage are unverified (CP-1A). | The largest rent source cannot be independently tested. | Rent durability | High | Obtain the guaranty and tenant financials |

| No investor presentation, ratings, market capitalisation or proxy ownership beyond two holders near 6% (CP-0, CP-1A). | No management guidance, agency view or market cross-check. | Context and sponsor alignment | Medium | Supply if wanted |

| Collateral and guarantors of the 8.625% secured notes due 2031 and the maturity month of the 2027 zero coupon notes are not stated in the pages read (CP-1). | Ranking and 2027 timing remain uncertain. | Subordination and maturity timing | Medium | Obtain indentures |

| Interim statements are unaudited and hotel statistics are manager-reported and unverified (CP-0, CP-1A). | Hotel KPIs and interim trends carry reliability risk. | Hotel findings | Medium | Cross-check to audited hotel revenue |
## Next module

Proceed to CP-5 (evidence trace). CP-5 should test that the figures used here resolve to the CP-1 and CP-1A handoffs, in particular the 9.78x and 1.41x metrics, the USD 1,586.9 million maturity total, the 62.9% and 40.5% secured shares, the 68.2% tenant share and the covenant sensitivities derived above, and that the stated limits on the EBITDA proxy and on revolver covenant headroom are carried into any later use.

### Cross-module consistency

The four handoffs tell one story with one exception. All use the same period labels (FY2025, Q1 to Q3 2026, nine months, LTM to Q3 2026), the same principal debt of 4,652,322, cash of 40,118, undrawn revolver of 650,000, LTM core EBITDA of 475,642 and ratios of 9.78x, 9.70x and 1.41x, and the same secured shares of 62.9% and 40.5%. The credit synthesis repeats the financial base and business context figures exactly. CP-1 corrected CP-0 on the revolver covenant terms and its correction is confirmed. The exception is the statement that debt service cover is the tighter test, repeated in CP-1 and CP-2 and corrected above. A definitional difference is recorded rather than resolved: the proxy EBITDA is not the indenture's income available for debt service, and the reported 1.83x test is not comparable with the 1.41x cover.
